paper.title: High Probability Bound for Cross-Learning Contextual Bandits with Unknown Context Distributions

settings.name_in_paper: Cross-learning contextual bandits with adversarial losses and i.i.d. contexts from an unknown distribution
unmapped: Cross-learning feedback: the learner observes the loss of the played arm under every context c in [C], not just the current context
Context distribution nu over a finite set [C] is unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: At the beginning of the problem, an oblivious adversary selects a sequence of losses $\ell_{t,c}(a) \in [0,1]$ for every round $t \in[T]$, every context $c \in [C]$, and every arm $a \in[K]$. In each round $t$, we begin by sampling a context $c_t \sim \nu$ i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\nu$ over $[C]$... Notably, the learner observes the loss for every context $c \in [C]$, but only for the arm $a_t$ they actually played.

algorithms.name: Algorithm of Schneider and Zimmert (2023) for cross-learning (epoch-based FTRL with estimated importance weights)

conditions: holds for any fixed policy pi: [C] -> [K]
tuning: L = sqrt(iota K T / log K)

source.label: thm:high_probability_main
source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, \Cref{alg:main} with parameters choice $\iota=2 \log (8 K T \frac{1}{\delta})$, $L=\sqrt{\frac{\iota K T}{\log (K)}}$, $\gamma=\frac{16 \iota}{L}$, and $\eta=\frac{\gamma}{2(2 L \gamma+\iota)}$  yields a regret bound of \[\Reg(\pi)= \widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{KT\log\frac{1}{\delta}} \right)\] with probability at least $1 - \delta$  for any policy $\pi$.

results.notes: Regret is the realized regret against a fixed policy pi, bounded with probability 1-delta. The algorithm is from Schneider & Zimmert (2023); the analysis is new. Computational efficiency is inferred from the paper calling it the first computationally efficient algorithm; the paper does not state compute for this theorem.
